knowledge:
- key_parameters: p.adj=adjusted p-value threshold for filtering significant gene sets in gm_filter ;; neg_NES=threshold for negative Normalized Enrichment Score filtering in gm_filter ;; pos_NES=threshold for positive Normalized Enrichment Score filtering in gm_filter ;; col_pos=color for positive enrichment in plots ;; col_neg=color for negative enrichment in plots ;; rect=logical to highlight clusters with rectangles in gm_dendplot ;; dend_len=height/length of the dendrogram in gm_dendplot ;; rect_len=size of the rectangles highlighting clusters in gm_dendplot ;; clust=logical indicating whether to plot by cluster or without clustering in enrichment functions ;; top=number of top enriched genes to plot in gm_enrichcores ;; output=name of the generated PDF report file in gm_enrichreport
- alternatives: clusterProfiler (specifically its GSEA function) is mentioned as the default tool to generate the input GSEA results. Other tools rely on hierarchically structured Gene Ontology (GO) classifications to reduce redundancy, but GSEAmining is preferred when using non-GO collections (such as MSigDB) which lack hierarchical organization.
- when_to_use: Use when you have performed GSEA (especially with MSigDB collections) and obtained a large number of enriched gene sets, and you want to group them into biologically meaningful clusters based on shared leading-edge genes to simplify interpretation.
- pitfalls: The input data frame must contain at least three specific columns: ID, NES, and core_enrichment (where genes are slash-separated). If too many gene sets are passed without filtering via gm_filter, the clustering and visualizations will be cluttered and difficult to interpret. In gm_enrichcores, if multiple genes share the same frequency as the threshold set by top, all of them will be displayed, potentially expanding the plot.

workflows.name: gsea_clustering_and_visualization
workflows.intent: Filter, cluster, and visualize GSEA results based on leading-edge gene similarity, and generate a comprehensive PDF report.
input: gsea_results.csv (A data frame containing GSEA results with at least ID, NES, and core_enrichment columns)
workflows.stages: 1. Filter GSEA results using gm_filter ;; 2. Perform hierarchical clustering of gene sets using gm_clust ;; 3. Plot the cluster dendrogram using gm_dendplot ;; 4. Visualize enriched terms in gene set names per cluster using gm_enrichterms ;; 5. Visualize enriched genes in leading edge subsets per cluster using gm_enrichcores ;; 6. Generate a comprehensive PDF report using gm_enrichreport
workflows.code:
data("genesets_sel", package = 'GSEAmining')
gs.filt <- gm_filter(genesets_sel, 
                     p.adj = 0.05, 
                     neg_NES = 2.6, 
                     pos_NES = 2)
gs.cl <- gm_clust(gs.filt)
gm_dendplot(gs.filt, 
            gs.cl)
gm_dendplot(gs.filt, 
            gs.cl, 
            col_pos = 'orange', 
            col_neg = 'black', 
            rect = TRUE,
            dend_len = 20, 
            rect_len = 2)
gm_enrichterms(gs.filt, gs.cl)
gm_enrichterms(gs.filt, 
               gs.cl, 
               clust = FALSE,
               col_pos = 'chocolate3',
               col_neg = 'skyblue3')
gm_enrichcores(gs.filt, gs.cl)
gm_enrichreport(gs.filt, gs.cl, output = 'gm_report')
